q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most. Of 52 small-channel videos with a baseline, 34.6% outperformed, with an average relative lift of 5.4. Mid channels come next: 23.1% of 39 videos, lift 1.6. Large channels trail: 5.3% of 19 videos, lift 1.0.

On happiness, all three groups lean positive, but unevenly. Mid-size audiences are happiest at +34 net (53.1% positive, 19.6% negative, n=450 product-side comments). Small channels are at +26 (48.4% positive, 22.1% negative, n=688). Large channels are lowest at +11 (43.6% positive, 32.1% negative, n=280).

Caveat: the large group is small, with only 19 videos having a baseline out of 25. The small group's high average lift may be driven by a few big hits. These patterns are associations, not causes.
sql: WITH vid AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' ELSE 'large' END AS size_group, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id LEFT JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), lift AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM vid GROUP BY size_group), sent AS (SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN vid v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY v.size_group) SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative, CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=l.size_group ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions clearly work best for mid-sized channels. Across 18 videos, they average a relative lift of 2.38, and 44% outperformed. Net sentiment is +34 (n=242 product-side comments).

Other formats trail, and most have very small samples:
- Explainer/tips (6 videos): lift 1.13, 17% outperformed, sentiment +7 (n=82).
- Comparison (3 videos): lift 1.70, none outperformed, sentiment +13 (n=48).
- Upgrade advice (6 videos): lift 0.65, none outperformed, but sentiment +46 (n=59).
- Keynote recap (2 videos): lift 0.60, none outperformed, sentiment +9 (n=23).
- Other (3 videos) and meme/short (1 video) are too small to read.

Caveat: only first impressions has a meaningful sample, and these are associations, not proof that the format causes the lift.
sql: WITH vids AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' AND p.rel_lift IS NOT NULL), perf AS (SELECT format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate FROM vids GROUP BY format), sent AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(m.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(m.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM vids v JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=v.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT p.format, p.n_videos, p.avg_rel_lift, p.outperformer_rate, s.n_product_side, CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(s.n_pos-s.n_neg)/s.n_product_side,3) END AS net_sentiment FROM perf p LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.format=p.format ORDER BY p.outperformer_rate DESC, p.avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
The two most negative high-lift videos are both from Shawn Shaman, and neither is strongly negative.

1. "Apple Tricked You With iPhone Duo" (meme short): net sentiment -7 (n=14; 43% positive, 50% negative). Lift is 118.42 (relative lift 9.5) on 181,178 views.

2. "Don't Buy The #iPhoneDuo... Here's Why" (upgrade advice): net sentiment 0 (n=16; 31% positive, 31% negative). Lift is 135.83 (relative lift 10.9) on 207,822 views.

Both videos draw big reach with a roughly split or mildly negative reaction. Both samples are small (14 and 16 product-side comments), so a few comments could shift the scores a lot. Lift and sentiment here are associations, not causes.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(1.0*s.pos/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(1.0*s.neg/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(1.0*(s.pos-s.neg)/s.n_product_side,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND s.n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC LIMIT 2

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Praise for the video is the largest topic (n=208, 13.1% of tagged comments). Samsung Fold comparisons is second (n=141, 8.9%), followed by Cases and design (n=113, 7.1%).

Samsung Fold comparisons is also growing fastest, up 353% week over week (15 to 68 comments). Next are Cases and design, up 229% (17 to 56), Apple's approach and Android, up 187% (15 to 43), and Reasons not to buy, up 180% (10 to 28).

Pre-order plans (9 to 33) and Buy or don't buy (6 to 33) also jumped. Their prior-week counts are under 10, so they have no growth rate and the jumps rest on small numbers.

Caveat: these counts come from a sample of comments, so they show what commenters discuss, not the wider audience.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS dy FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.topic_id IS NOT NULL), mx AS (SELECT MAX(dy) AS d FROM base), agg AS (SELECT b.topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN b.dy > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN b.dy BETWEEN mx.d-13 AND mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM base b, mx GROUP BY b.topic_id), r AS (SELECT a.*, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/(SELECT SUM(n_total) FROM agg),3) AS share_of_tagged, n_this_week - n_prev_week AS abs_change, CASE WHEN n_prev_week>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(n_this_week-n_prev_week)/n_prev_week,3) END AS wow_growth FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id) SELECT topic_id, name, pool, origin, first_seen, n_total, share_of_tagged, n_this_week, n_prev_week, abs_change, wow_growth, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY n_total DESC) AS size_rank, CASE WHEN wow_growth IS NOT NULL THEN RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY (wow_growth IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY wow_growth DESC) END AS growth_rank FROM r ORDER BY n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo is clearly the most positively received topic, at a net sentiment of +26 (49% positive, 23% negative, n=1,418 product-side comments across 127 videos). 

The other topics trail it:
- Competitor foldables: +9 (39% positive, 30% negative), but only n=23 across 2 videos.
- Other: -10 (31% positive, 41% negative, n=51, 6 videos).
- General event videos: -15 (26% positive, 41% negative, n=76, 8 videos).
- iPhone 18 Pro: n=3, so there's no usable score.

Duo's figure rests on a large sample. The other topics have small samples, so treat their scores as rough directional signals. These are comments on a sample of videos, so they may not represent the wider audience.
sql: SELECT c.topic AS topic, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY net_sentiment DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
People like the fold animation most. It has the best net sentiment, +70 (n=56, 84% positive, 14% negative), though the sample is fairly small. Eager-to-buy comments are also strongly positive at +38 (n=104). Comparisons with the Samsung Fold draw the most positive comments (79 of 141, net +31).

Criticism centres on price and on how Duo stacks up against alternatives. High price has net +15 (n=102, 32% negative, 33 negative comments). Duo versus iPhone 18 Pro Max is nearly split at +2 (n=101, 32% negative). Reasons not to buy is +5 (n=55), a smaller sample. Samsung Fold comparisons also have the most negative comments (36), but net sentiment there is still positive.

Caveat: topics overlap, so the same comments appear in both lists, and this is only a sample of comments.
sql: WITH t AS (SELECT tp.topic_id, tp.name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM comments c JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics tp ON tp.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND tp.pool='product' GROUP BY tp.topic_id, tp.name) SELECT side, name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(n_pos*1.0/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(n_neg*1.0/n,3) AS neg_share FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, * FROM (SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8)) UNION ALL SELECT side, name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(n_pos*1.0/n,3), ROUND(n_neg*1.0/n,3) FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, * FROM (SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8)) LIMIT 40
